---
title: "Evaluate inference (classification)"
---

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_notebooks.py from cookbook/recipes/eval_inference/example.py — edit the recipe, not this page. -->

Run a classifier over a registered source and score its predictions
against gold labels.

**When to use this pattern.** You have a labelled holdout set and you
want a single number — accuracy, macro F1, per-class F1 — to compare
two classifiers, or to track drift over time on the same classifier.

## API surface exercised

- `Session.eval_inference(*, model, source, columns, task, ground_truth, label_column)`

The returned dict carries `aggregate` (tagged by `"task"` — currently
`"classification"`) with `accuracy`, `f1`, and `per_class`, plus
`per_record` (one entry per aligned `{record_id, predicted, gold}`).

The `task` argument is the string form of the inference task —
`"classification"` here. For NER, see `../eval_inference_ner/`.

## Ground-truth source shape

`eval_inference` requires a registered source with these columns:

| column            | type | example   |
|-------------------|------|-----------|
| `id`              | utf8 | `"1"`     |
| `<label_column>`  | utf8 | `physics` |

`label_column` is the kwarg you pass at call time — `label` in this
recipe. Every `id` in the ground-truth source must resolve to a row in the
input source; rows without a gold label are silently dropped from the
metric.

The program is [`cookbook/recipes/eval_inference/example.py`](https://github.com/f-inverse/jammi-ai/blob/main/cookbook/recipes/eval_inference/example.py); its steps run here in order.

```{python}
import tempfile

import jammi
from jammi_cookbook import fixtures

MODEL = "distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased-finetuned-sst-2-english"

db = jammi.connect(f"file://{tempfile.mkdtemp()}")
```

The classifier is DistilBERT fine-tuned on SST-2, the Stanford sentiment
treebank, from the Hugging Face Hub: it labels a text `POSITIVE` or
`NEGATIVE`, and its label names are read from the checkpoint's own
`config.json`.

## Register the reviews and the gold labels

The corpus is 24 short product and service reviews, half of each sentiment;
the gold source is one `(id, label)` row per review.

```{python}
db.add_source("reviews", url=str(fixtures.path("tiny_reviews.parquet")), format="parquet")
db.add_source("truth", url=str(fixtures.path("tiny_review_labels.csv")), format="csv")
```

## Run the classifier and score it

`eval_inference` runs the model over `columns`, aligns each prediction with
its gold label by `id`, and returns the scores: `aggregate` holds accuracy
and macro F1 (F1 averaged over the classes), tagged with the task.

```{python}
metrics = db.eval_inference(
    model=MODEL,
    source="reviews",
    columns=["text"],
    task="classification",
    ground_truth="truth.public.tiny_review_labels",
    label_column="label",
)

aggregate = metrics["aggregate"]
assert aggregate["task"] == "classification", aggregate["task"]
print(f"accuracy:  {aggregate['accuracy']:.4f}")
print(f"macro_f1:  {aggregate['f1']:.4f}")
assert aggregate["accuracy"] > 0.5, "half the reviews are each sentiment, so a coin scores 0.5"
```

## Read the breakdowns

`aggregate["per_class"]` scores each label on its own; `per_record` holds one
aligned prediction and gold label per row, so the reviews the model got wrong
can be read. A review that reports relief in negative words is the kind of
text a sentiment model trips on.

```{python}
per_class = aggregate.get("per_class", {})
assert isinstance(per_class, dict), f"per_class shape: {type(per_class)}"
for label, stats in per_class.items():
    print(
        f"{label:<12} precision={stats['precision']:.4f}"
        f"  recall={stats['recall']:.4f}  f1={stats['f1']:.4f}"
    )

per_record = metrics["per_record"]
assert len(per_record) == 24, "one aligned prediction per review"
texts = {
    str(row["id"]): row["text"]
    for row in db.sql("SELECT id, text FROM reviews.public.tiny_reviews").to_pylist()
}
misses = [r for r in per_record if r["predicted"] != r["gold"]]
for miss in misses:
    print(f"missed {miss['record_id']}: {texts[miss['record_id']]!r}")
    print(f"  predicted {miss['predicted']}, gold {miss['gold']}")
assert len(misses) == round((1 - aggregate["accuracy"]) * len(per_record))
```

## The predictions alone

Without gold labels, `infer` runs the model over a source and returns one
row per source row, keyed by `key` (as text, in `_row_id`): the label, the
probability the model gave it, and every label's score. They are the labels
`eval_inference` scored.

```{python}
predictions = db.infer(
    source="reviews",
    model=MODEL,
    columns=["text"],
    task="classification",
    key="id",
)
assert predictions.num_rows == 24, predictions.num_rows
rows = predictions.select(["_row_id", "label", "confidence"]).to_pylist()
for row in rows[:4]:
    print(f"{row['label']:<9} {row['confidence']:.3f}  {texts[row['_row_id']]!r}")
scored = {r["record_id"]: r["predicted"] for r in per_record}
assert all(row["label"] == scored[row["_row_id"]] for row in rows)
assert all(row["confidence"] >= 0.5 for row in rows), "a two-label top choice holds at least half"
```

```{python}
db.close()
```
